newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO may rebound on crude gains-traders.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO may rebound on crude gains-traders.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Friday were expected to rebound on stronger crude prices, traders said.
They said rumours were also heard that a local trader may be interested to see higher prices as he "price out" cargoes.
Bids/offers on Thursday were indicated between $116-$118 per tonne on a free-on-board basis from Singapore.
December Brent was last traded at $23.95 per barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange, a 20 cents gain.
But paper indications were lower in the swaps market. November was bid/asked at $117.50/$118 per tonne lower from Thursday's quotes at $118/$118.50 per tonne.
Traders said while crude may pull prices higher, cash fundamentals remained bearish.
They said the bunker market was not providing enough support. Pockets of demand were seen from China but bids remained low. -- Singapore newsroom (+65-870-3082)
